sources.title: Kia EV3 MY27 Australian specification sheet
sources.supports: Four FWD grades. Pack energy 58.3/81.4 kWh and battery weight 375/470 kg; boot 460 L, frunk 25 L; towing 500/1,000 kg braked; smart-key fob, no Digital Key, no rear seat heating, no heat pump, no Remote Smart Parking Assist row; Utility Mode, V2L and Lead Vehicle Departure Alert standard.

sources.title: Kia EV5 Australian specification sheet
sources.supports: Pack energy 64.2/88.1 kWh and battery weight 428/573/574 kg; cargo 513 L seats up and 1,714 L seats down (VDA); frunk 67 L; GT-Line-only Remote Smart Park Assist 2, heated rear seats and heated steering wheel; no factory dashcam, Digital Key or heat pump row.

sources.title: Kia EV3 Australian owner's manual (737 pages, full-text search)
sources.supports: No walk-away locking, Pet Mode, cabin overheat protection, built-in camera recording, garage opener or traffic-light alert. Doors relock 30 seconds after an unused unlock. Digital Key 2, Approach Unlock and Remote Smart Parking Assist are marked 'if equipped'. Leading Vehicle Departure Alert p. 481; Utility Mode p. 25; Auto Comfort Control for the driver's seat p. 280 (if equipped).

sources.title: Kia EV5 Australian owner's manual (740 pages, full-text search)
sources.supports: No walk-away locking, Pet Mode, cabin overheat protection, built-in camera recording, garage opener or traffic-light alert. Leading Vehicle Departure Alert p. 467; Utility Mode p. 26; approach unlock with the smart key p. 188.

sources.title: Kia EV3 GT-Line AWD Australian launch report
sources.supports: A$66,490 plus on-road costs; September 2026; dual motor 195 kW/385 Nm; 0-100 km/h 6.6 s; 81.4 kWh; up to 559 km WLTP; larger brakes and Australian suspension tune.

sources.title: Kia EV3 AWD confirmed for Australia
sources.supports: GT-Line AWD equipment: 19-inch wheels, head-up display, heated and ventilated front seats, heated steering wheel, V2L, wireless phone projection, OTA updates, powered driver's seat and tailgate.

sources.title: 2027 Kia EV3 GT-Line AWD specification record
sources.supports: Kerb weight 1,995 kg; luggage 460 L; front compartment 25 L. Overseas database record, not a Kia Australia document.

sources.title: Kia EV3 Long Range
sources.supports: Fast-charge peak 135 kW; cargo 460 L, 1,251 L maximum; 25 L front; 1,000 kg braked towing; heat pump optional by country. European record.

sources.title: Kia EV3 Standard Range
sources.supports: Fast-charge peak 100 kW; 10-80% about 30 minutes. European record.

sources.title: 2026 Kia EV5 review
sources.supports: Long Range maximum DC charge rate 140 kW; 513 L boot, 1,714 L folded, 67 L frunk; 7-year vehicle and 7-year/150,000 km battery warranty.

sources.title: 2025 Kia EV3 review
sources.supports: Reports that no heat pump is available for Australia, even as an option.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 2 Australian specification sheet (visually inspected)
sources.supports: Boot 380 L, 1,320 L maximum; no front boot row; heat pump, NFC card key, BYD digital key and Bluetooth key standard on both grades; no heated steering wheel or rear seat heating row; 82 kW DC; no tow rating row.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 2 Australian owner's handbook (210 pages, full-text search)
sources.supports: Towing 750 kg maximum with the towing function fitted (p. 94). No walk-away locking, Pet Mode, parked recording, cabin overheat protection, remote parking, garage opener, traffic-light alert, automatic seat climate or cloud driver profiles.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 3 EVO Australian owner's handbooks, Premium and Dynamic (full-text search)
sources.supports: Towing table 1,500 kg braked (Premium, p. 102). No walk-away locking, Pet Mode, parked recording, cabin overheat protection, remote parking, garage opener, traffic-light alert, automatic seat climate or cloud driver profiles.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 3 Australian specification sheet
sources.supports: Luggage 440 L minimum, 1,340 L maximum; no front boot; 750 kg braked towing; heated front seats listed, no ventilation, rear seat heating or steering-wheel heating row; built-in dash camera row.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 3 Australian owner's handbook (210 pages, full-text search)
sources.supports: START/STOP button operation; driving recorder with SD card (p. 146). No walk-away locking, Pet Mode, parked recording, cabin overheat protection, remote parking, garage opener, traffic-light alert or navigation-triggered battery conditioning.

sources.title: BYD SEALION 7 overseas product page
sources.supports: Overseas figure of 1,789 L with the rear seats folded (520 L seats-up basis). BYD Australia publishes 500 L rear and 58 L front only.

sources.title: BYD guide to charging times
sources.supports: ATTO 3 60.48 kWh: 30-80% in about 29 minutes at up to 88 kW DC. UK publication.

sources.title: BYD Australia referral program page
sources.supports: Page shows only the heading 'BYD Referral Program - Join the BYD Family'. No reward, eligibility or expiry terms are published.

sources.title: ANCAP safety ratings register search
sources.supports: BYD entries: ATTO 1, ATTO 3, SEAL 6, SEALION 7, SHARK 6 and M9. No ATTO 2 entry. Jaecoo: J7 only, no J5 entry.

sources.title: BYD ATTO 3 ANCAP rating
sources.supports: Five stars, 2022 datestamp, expires December 2028. 'Applies to: All Australian variants', build dates May 2022 onwards; the narrative names Standard Range and Extended Range variants. EVO is not named.

sources.title: Geely EX5 2026 Australian brochure and specification guide
sources.supports: Luggage 302 L (410 L expanded), 1,877 L second row down; no front storage listed; proximity key; first-row seat heating only; heated steering wheel; heat pump A/C; Camping Space; full driver-assistance suite standard on both grades; towing preparation harness.

sources.title: Geely EX5 tow-rating approval report
sources.supports: Every EX5 variant on sale, including the three 68.39 kWh approvals, is rated 0 kg braked and unbraked. Two new towbar variants were filed (750 kg) but are not on sale.

sources.title: Geely EX5 dash cam guide
sources.supports: Reports that overseas EX5s have a factory driving recorder and sentry mode, and that Australian-delivered cars arrived without them switched on.

sources.title: 2026 Geely EX5 review
sources.supports: Heat pump standard; 302-410 L boot, 1,877 L folded; walk-away locking present but inconsistent; 100 kW DC, 30-80% in 20 minutes.

sources.title: Zeekr 7X user manual, Australian owner mirror (429 pages, full-text search)
sources.supports: Approach unlock and walk-away lock p. 44; Sentry Mode with recording pp. 317-319; Pet Mode p. 320; Camping Mode pp. 320-321; charging-point battery preheating p. 337; position memory for seats, mirrors, wheel and HUD p. 70, three driving positions per ZEEKR ID p. 185; auto-fold mirrors on lock p. 40; automatic steering-wheel heating p. 159. No driving recorder, garage opener, cabin overheat protection, automatic seat climate or traffic-light alert.

sources.title: Zeekr 7X Australian brochure - cargo
sources.supports: 'Electric boot access with up to 1978L of space'; 62 L frunk, stated for the RWD version.

sources.title: Zeekr 7X Performance AWD 2026 review
sources.supports: Reported 42 L front storage on the dual-motor car, against 62 L on rear-drive versions.

sources.title: Jaecoo J5 EV Australian specification sheet, edition 1.01
sources.supports: Two proximity keys, passive entry and start, walk-away auto locking, remote start; heated and ventilated front seats only; no heated steering wheel, heat pump, dashcam, phone key, navigation or optional pack listed; luggage 384 L to cover, 480 L to roof.

sources.title: Jaecoo J5 EV review
sources.supports: Describes a dedicated Pet Mode that keeps climate control running for short periods and shows a message to people outside.

sources.title: Jaecoo J5 EV review
sources.supports: 480 L boot and a 35 L frunk with drain plug; a regenerative-braking fix was expected by OTA update.

sources.title: 2026 Jaecoo J5 EV review
sources.supports: 384 L boot, 1,180 L with the rear seats folded, 35 L front boot.

sources.title: 2026 Jaecoo J5 EV review
sources.supports: Reports that the Jaecoo app pre-conditions the cabin, shows charge status and schedules charging; proximity unlocking must be enabled in the multimedia system.

sources.title: 2026 Jaecoo J5 EV review
sources.supports: ANCAP: not tested.

sources.title: 2026 BYD ATTO 2 local review
sources.supports: The ATTO 2 has not been crash-tested by ANCAP.

sources.title: Model Y Australian manual - towing and accessories
sources.supports: Five-seat and Performance: 1,588 kg. Six-seat: 3,500 lb with four or fewer occupants (printed as 1,558 kg; 3,500 lb is 1,588 kg), reducing to 1,043 kg with six occupants. Separate trailer brakes recommended above 750 kg.

sources.title: Model Y and Model 3 Australian manuals - subsystems
sources.supports: Rear motor: AC permanent-magnet synchronous. Front motor on AWD vehicles: AC induction. High-voltage battery: liquid-cooled lithium-ion, 345 V (Model Y) and 355 V (Model 3) nominal. No capacity, mass or motor output is published.

sources.title: Model 3 Australian manual - dimensions and cargo
sources.supports: Front trunk 88 L; behind second row 594 L; maximum total with five passengers 682 L. No folded-seat volume is published.

sources.title: Model 3 Tow Package, Tesla Australia shop
sources.supports: Up to 1,000 kg; 750 kg without a brake controller. 'Compatible with all non-performance Model 3 variants'.

sources.title: Tesla Australia - FSD (Supervised) feature table
sources.supports: Dumb Summon and Actually Smart Summon are both marked 'Upcoming' in Australia. The Australian manual says Summon may be inactive on vehicles built from about mid-February 2024 until a future update.

sources.title: Tesla Model 3 Australian configurator - Rear-Wheel Drive feature list
sources.supports: A$45,900, 572 km WLTP, 6.2 s. Interior list: textile and vegan leather seats, heated first-row seats, manual-folding second row. No heated steering wheel is listed.

sources.title: Tesla Model Y 2026 price and specifications data
sources.supports: Industry data feed, not a Tesla publication: battery 60 kWh (Rear-Wheel Drive), 79 kWh (Premium Long Range and L), 84.7 kWh (Performance); front motor 158 kW; rear motor 220 kW (Premium Long Range), 208 kW (L), 303 kW (Performance).

sources.title: Tesla Model Y and Model 3 records
sources.supports: European estimates: Model Y 10-80% in about 27-28 minutes; Model 3 RWD 60 kWh usable, 175 kW peak, about 24 minutes; Model 3 Long Range and Performance 79 kWh usable, about 28 minutes. Not Australian-build measurements.

sources.title: Tesla Model 3 2026 Long Range RWD report
sources.supports: Reports a 78.4 kWh LG NMC pack for the 750 km Long Range RWD and a 62.5 kWh LFP pack for the 520 km RWD.
